reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: A metabolic combined immunodeficiency in which a predominantly T-cell defect is accompanied by prominent, and often presenting, neurological disease
Neurological features include developmental delay, spasticity, motor abnormalities and ataxia, which may precede overt infection
Recurrent and opportunistic infections reflect progressive T-cell depletion, while B-cell numbers are relatively preserved though antibody function may decline over time
Autoimmune phenomena such as autoimmune haemolytic anaemia and thrombocytopenia are frequently associated
A characteristic biochemical clue is markedly low serum and urinary uric acid due to the metabolic block, which can prompt the diagnosis
It is closely related to adenosine deaminase deficiency as one of the two classic purine salvage pathway defects causing immunodeficiency
Inheritance is autosomal recessive from biallelic loss-of-function variants in the PNP gene
Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation can correct the immunodeficiency but established neurological damage is not reversed
reference.pathophysiology: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase is an enzyme of the purine salvage pathway that catalyses the breakdown of inosine, guanosine and deoxyguanosine. Its deficiency causes accumulation of deoxyguanosine triphosphate, which is particularly toxic to developing and dividing T lymphocytes, producing a progressive T-cell lymphopenia and combined immunodeficiency while sparing B-cell numbers more than adenosine deaminase deficiency. The same toxic metabolites are thought to injure the central nervous system, accounting for the developmental and motor abnormalities. The metabolic block also diverts purines away from uric acid production, giving the characteristic hypouricaemia.
additionalDifferentials: Other forms of severe combined immunodeficiency
Inherited metabolic and mitochondrial disorders with neurological involvement
additionalInvestigations: Serum and urinary uric acid, characteristically very low
Red-cell or leucocyte PNP enzyme activity assay
Lymphocyte subsets showing progressive T-cell depletion with relatively preserved B cells
Serum immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses
Autoantibody screen and direct antiglobulin test
PNP gene sequencing for biallelic loss-of-function variants
redFlags: Opportunistic or disseminated infection indicating advanced T-cell failure
Complications from live vaccine exposure before diagnosis
Development of lymphoma or other malignancy
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is poor without treatment, with death from infection in childhood; haematopoietic stem cell transplantation can restore immune function, but the neurological impairment already present tends to persist and shapes the long-term outcome.
pitfalls: Attributing the neurological signs to cerebral palsy and overlooking the underlying immunodeficiency
Not checking uric acid, thereby missing a readily available diagnostic clue
Confusing it with adenosine deaminase deficiency without enzyme-specific testing
Administering live vaccines or non-irradiated blood products before the diagnosis is made
Assuming transplantation will reverse established neurological damage
references: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders in Infants and Children
IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
management: Offer allogeneic haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation as the only definitive treatment able to restore cellular immunity

Give infection prophylaxis against opportunistic organisms including co-trimoxazole for Pneumocystis with antifungal and antiviral cover, and immunoglobulin replacement where antibody function declines
Use only irradiated, cytomegalovirus-safe, leucodepleted blood products and withhold live vaccines given the T-cell defect
Treat associated autoimmune haemolytic anaemia and cytopenias with corticosteroids and further immunosuppression
Provide neurological supportive care for spasticity, developmental delay and seizures through paediatric neurology and therapy services
Monitor for intercurrent and opportunistic infection and, after transplantation, track immune reconstitution
Refer for genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive inheritance
